title: All given by one Shepherd
summary: Rabbi Yehoshua calls a teaching "a pearl": Hashem, Klal Yisrael and Shabbos each testify to the other. Words of Torah are like a goad that guides and a nail that stays fixed, and opposing opinions in Torah were all given by one Shepherd. Then Yosef's "I am Yosef" that left his brothers speechless, Shaul and Shmuel at Ein Dor, and the verses that made the Amoraim cry.
key_ideas: Opposing opinions in Torah were all given by one Shepherd, so each deserves to be understood.
Words of Torah are like a goad that guides a person and a nail that stays fixed.
Yosef's "I am Yosef" left his brothers unable to answer; how much more so the judgment of the future.
The Amoraim cried at verses about judgment, from Yosef's brothers to Shmuel's ascent at Ein Dor.
